chief_complaint: unbearable nocturnal itching and finger web burrows
hpi_details: A 62-year-old female presents to the clinic with unbearable nocturnal itching and finger web burrows. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks she might have brought home bedbugs from a roadside motel she stayed at during a family road trip last month.
concerns: She is worried she will pass a contagious bug to her newborn granddaughter whom she babysits three days a week.
expectations: She hopes to receive a strong prescription cream or sleeping aid so she can finally sleep through the night without scratching.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Scabies is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Scabies: Topical Permethrin 5% cream full body (repeat in 7 days), treat family, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Scabies.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Eczema without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Widespread crusted, hyperkeratotic lesions with minimal itch in an elderly or immunocompromised patient — think crusted (Norwegian) scabies, which is highly contagious.

Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.one_liner: A mite infestation causing intense nocturnal itching with burrows in the finger webs.
red_flags: Widespread crusted, hyperkeratotic lesions with minimal itch in an elderly or immunocompromised patient — think crusted (Norwegian) scabies, which is highly contagious
Signs of secondary bacterial infection (cellulitis, impetiginization) — risk of post-streptococcal complications

must_ask.say: Is the itching worse at night?
Where is the itching worst — between your fingers?
Has anyone around you had similar itching?
How long has this been going on?
Have you seen any thin lines on your skin?

history.answer: Doctor, the itching between my fingers is unbearable, especially at night when I try to sleep.
It began about two weeks ago and has been getting steadily worse each day.
It started in the skin between my fingers, and over the past week small red bumps have spread to my wrists, waist, and inner thighs.
It is most severe between my fingers, around my inner wrists, around my belly button, and along my inner thighs.
I see tiny, thread-like wavy lines between my fingers along with small red pimples and scratch marks.
The itch is relentless, but it flares up intensely at night under warm bedcovers, keeping me up for hours.
No, the bumps remain in the same places continuously rather than coming and going within hours.
I have never had any skin problem like this before.
I have not had any fever or chills, though I feel worn out and exhausted from not being able to sleep.
No sores, redness, or blisters in my mouth, eyes, or private areas.
My skin does not feel painful or peel off, and I do not have any purple spots or dark bruises.
No swelling of my face, lips, or tongue, and no breathing difficulty or dizziness.
I haven't started any new prescription drugs, antibiotics, gout pills, or painkillers.
I haven't changed my laundry detergent, soaps, or lotions, and I haven't handled any plants or new metal jewelry.
Yes, my husband started itching around his waist a few days ago, and my grandson whom I watch has also been scratching his hands.
I volunteered at a nursing care home last month, but I haven't gone hiking, had insect bites, or traveled recently.
No, I have never had eczema, asthma, or allergic rhinitis.
My joints do not hurt or swell, and my fingernails look completely normal.
I put an over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream on my hands, but it didn't help at all and might have made the itching worse.
I have been married and monogamous with my husband for thirty years, with no history of genital ulcers or sores.
I was wondering if I brought home bedbugs from that motel we stayed at last month during our family trip.
I'm so worried that whatever this is, I might pass it on to my newborn granddaughter when I babysit her.
I just hope you can give me a strong prescription lotion or something to knock out the itching so I can actually sleep tonight.
I do not have any chronic medical conditions like high blood pressure or diabetes.
I had an appendectomy thirty years ago, but no other operations or hospital stays.
I do not take any prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, or vitamins.
I have no known allergies to medications, foods, or anything else.
I have never smoked cigarettes.
I only drink a glass of wine socially once or twice a month.
I am a retired homemaker living with my husband, and I babysit my young grandson three afternoons a week.
There is no family history of psoriasis, autoimmune skin diseases, or chronic skin conditions.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 124/78 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, temperature 36.7 C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert, tired-appearing woman who is actively scratching her wrists and hands, with no acute respiratory distress.
Conjunctivae are pink and non-injected, and sclerae are anicteric without mucosal lesions.
Oral mucosa is pink and moist without erythema, erosions, blisters, or ulcerations.
No cervical, axillary, or epitrochlear lymphadenopathy palpable.

Multiple fine, wavy serpiginous burrows and small erythematous papules in bilateral finger web spaces and flexor wrists, with scattered excoriations and no thick crusting or impetiginized purulent exudates.
No erythematous nodules, rash, or ulcerations on the external genitalia.
